headline: Bell calls its Nov 17 breach a separate attack from the email outage, and says Bell MTS customers' data was hit in that breach.
summary: Correction: c009 quoted the Free Press as saying the cyberattack "also targeted" Bell Canada's systems and called the wording unclear on whether it was one attack. The story says "a separate cyberattack also targeted Bell Canada's internal systems"; c009 and q003's answer now say so. New source s007: CBC News (Nov 23, read on Radio Canada International's copy), where a Bell spokesperson says customers with Bell, Bell Aliant, Bell MTS, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile were affected after an 'agentic threat actor' accessed some Bell internal systems on Nov 17; new c013 (Reported), timeline t007. It does not mention email, so q003 stays Not established. Re-read CBC (s005, behind c003): Bell MTS said service was restored on Nov 20; service stays back. Re-read the Free Press (s001): unchanged. No Bell MTS own-channel notice, no second outlet with its own cyberattack statement, no count, no attacker; q001 stays Reported, q002 and q004 open. No rumors found. Staleness check done: q003 not_known line and checked-not-found note updated. Not eligible for resolved: this is an update.

headline: Bell MTS says a cyberattack caused its email outage. One outlet so far; Reported.
summary: New incident page. Sources read: Winnipeg Free Press (Nov 22 and Nov 20), CBC (two stories), BleepingComputer, the Globe and Mail (Tier 2). Main question: Reported, because the Nov 22 statement reaches us through one outlet and Bell has not posted it on its own channels. The Bell Canada Nov 17 breach is covered here only as context; it is not on the site as its own page yet. Scale and attacker: Not established. Status monitoring.
